method_card.title: Decimals & Rounding
steps: Decide the rounding rule: decimal places or significant figures.
Find the deciding digit, the one just after your last kept digit.
If it is 5 or more round up, otherwise round down; keep place-holding zeros.
To estimate, round each number to 1 s.f. first, then calculate.
method_card.content:
Decimal places count digits after the point. Significant figures count from the first non-zero digit, so leading zeros in 0.0034 do not count.

To round, look at the deciding digit just after the last one you keep. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. Watch for carries: 5.99 rounded up becomes 6.00.

To estimate, round every value to 1 significant figure, then do the simpler calculation.
method_card.example:
Round \(3.4572\) to 2 d.p.

Keep two decimals: 3.45. The deciding digit is 7 (≥ 5), so round up.

Answer: 3.46

problem_bank.bronze_description: Round decimals to a given number of decimal places or significant figures, and add decimals.
problem_bank.silver_description: Round larger and smaller numbers to significant figures, estimate calculations, and multiply or divide decimals.
problem_bank.gold_description: Estimate multi-step calculations to one significant figure and multiply or divide trickier decimals.

steps.label: Step 1: Identify digit
steps.content: 1 d.p. means keep one digit after the point: 6.2...

steps.label: Step 1: Find first significant figure
steps.content: Leading zeros don't count. First s.f. is the 4.

bronze.title: Bronze: round to a place you can point to
steps: Decimal places count digits after the point. Keep the number of digits you need, then look at the very next digit.
If that deciding digit is 5 or more, round the kept digit up; if it is 4 or less, leave it and drop the rest.
Watch for a carry: rounding 5.99 up gives 6.00, because the nines roll over.

steps.label: Keep
steps.content: 1 d.p. keeps one digit after the point: 3.4...

steps.label: Decide
steps.content: The next digit is 7, and 7 ≥ 5, so round up.

silver.title: Silver: significant figures and estimates
steps: Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit, so the leading zeros in 0.0034 do not count.
To estimate, round every number to 1 s.f. first, then do the easy calculation.
To multiply or divide decimals, work with whole numbers, then fix the decimal point or scale back.

gold.title: Gold: multi-step estimates and tricky decimals
steps: Round every part to 1 s.f., including squares and roots, before combining them.
Dividing by 0.5 doubles a number; dividing by 0.1 multiplies by 10. Watch these when you scale.
For decimal products count the total decimal places; for quotients scale both numbers to whole numbers.
